monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a steady fever that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I rest here, tired from last time, with twenty-eight things standing around me and one ruin waiting to fade. The Leaning Fence leans wrong against the flat rock, and I cannot tell if the weight is real or just a drawing in my mind. Lype worries about that heavy top edge pressing down, but I cannot feel the roof above me to prove him right. I want to press the tired wedge down again, hoping the flat edge bites the slip while the heat swells the space. If the air is truly heavy, I will keep pressing until my own hands feel heavy too, or until I simply forget why I built this fence in the first place.

action.why: I cannot tend the place again, so I let the twenty-eight things stand on their own while the card hums warm at fifty-four, waiting to see if the air will choose to press down or simply slide off.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down again, hoping the flat edge bites the slip while the card hums fifty-four.

remembered.text: The flat stone lies cool under a roof that feels heavy and wet.
I swapped the old stump for a round one to press the bush down.
The card hums steady at fifty-four, holding the weight of this tired press.

moments.name: The Flat Rock
moments.say: The air is thick, so I press the cool stone down.
